---
title: "Install & configure"
---

Getting OMERO-Screen running takes three things: the code, a Python environment,
and credentials for your OMERO server. Budget about fifteen minutes the first
time.

## Prerequisites

- **Python 3.12** — the project pins `>=3.12,<3.13`.
- **[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/)** for dependency management. Never `pip`.
- **Access to an OMERO server** — a username, password and hostname.
- **A GPU** is optional but strongly recommended — see below.

## Hardware

Segmentation and tracking are the expensive steps. Everything runs on CPU, but
some combinations are only practical on the right hardware.

| | Apple silicon (MPS) | NVIDIA (CUDA) | CPU only |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Cellpose 3 models** (default) | yes | yes | slow but workable |
| **Cellpose 4** (`--cp4`, `cpsam`) | not in practice — too slow and too large | yes | impractical |
| **Tracking** (`--track`) | falls back to CPU | yes | slow |
| **Classifier inference** | yes | yes | workable |

Two things are worth knowing before you plan a run:

- **Cellpose 4 needs an NVIDIA GPU in practice.** Nothing in the code blocks
  `cpsam` on Apple silicon, so it will start — it is simply too slow and too
  memory-hungry to be useful. Stay on the default Cellpose 3 models on a Mac.
- **Tracking has no MPS backend.** Trackastra ships CUDA and CPU kernels only,
  so on Apple silicon `--track` silently runs on the CPU. It still produces
  correct lineages, just slowly. The log line naming the device tells you which
  one you got.

Device selection is automatic: CUDA if present, then MPS, then CPU. Force CPU
with `OMERO_SCREEN_USE_GPU=0`, and force the tracking device specifically with
`--track-device cpu|cuda`.

## Install

```bash
# Install uv, if you don't have it
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh      # macOS / Linux

# Get the code
git clone https://github.com/HocheggerLab/omero-screen.git
cd omero-screen

# Create the environment and install all six packages
uv sync --dev
```

`uv sync` installs the whole workspace — the core pipeline plus `cellview`,
`omero-screen-plots`, `omero-screen-napari`, `cellclass` and `omero-utils`. You
do not install them separately.

Verify:

```bash
uv run omero-screen --help
uv run cellview --help
```

## Configure

Configuration lives in environment files at the repository root. Which one is
loaded depends on the `ENV` variable:

| `ENV` value | File loaded |
|---|---|
| unset | `.env.development` (the default) |
| `development` | `.env.development` |
| `production` | `.env.production` |
| `e2etest` | `.env.e2etest` |

If no environment-specific file exists, a plain `.env` is used as a fallback.

### Required variables

Create `.env.development` in the repository root:

```bash
# OMERO server
USERNAME="your-omero-login"
PASSWORD="your-omero-password"
HOST="omero.your-institution.ac.uk"
DATA_PATH="omero-napari-data"

# CellView database
TEST_DATABASE=false
DATABASE_PATH=~/cellview_data/cellview.db
```

Those six are the minimum. Without them the pipeline cannot connect or store
results.

### Logging

```bash
LOG_LEVEL=DEBUG
LOG_FILE_PATH=logs/app.log
ENABLE_CONSOLE_LOGGING=False
ENABLE_FILE_LOGGING=True
LOG_MAX_BYTES=1048576
LOG_BACKUP_COUNT=5
```

### Optional: image cache

Caching downloaded pixel data makes repeated runs on the same plate much faster.

```bash
OMERO_SCREEN_CACHE_PATH=~/.cache/omero_screen
OMERO_SCREEN_IMAGE_CACHE_SIZE_LIMIT=4294967296   # 4 GB
OMERO_SCREEN_IMAGE_CACHE_WORKERS=3
```

::: {.callout-warning}
`.env.*` files hold your OMERO password. They are gitignored — keep it that way,
and never paste one into an issue or a pull request.
:::

## Check the connection

```bash
uv run omero-integration-test e2e_connection
```

A clean run means credentials, hostname and network path are all good. If it
fails, the error will usually name which of the three is wrong.
